Application Performance Management 9.60 patch versions before IP4 are affected. This issue seems to be present throughout the application, as several endpoints or functionalities that are restricted to Admin users can be directly accessed by Regular users. The authorization method of the application can be bypassed allowing users to perform unauthorized actions to their role. The application performs authorization checks to keep users from accessing functionality outside of their role such as create, verify, and/or repair. 




This authorization method can be bypassed. During VA testing, it was found that under the User Reports inside the Applications menu, it is possible to  create links and different reports. pages and the application allows them to further use these restricted functionalities.

In Application Performance Management versions before 9.60 IP4, The application is vulnerable to cross-site scripting wherein the application does not properly validate the input parameters, allowing scripts to be injected and then executed in the context of a user’s browser. This can lead to the attacker stealing sensitive information, impersonating users, or performing actions on their behalf.  Also, the application may also be vulnerable to the below attacks:

• Link Injection – This occurs when an attacker inserts a malicious link into a webpage, often in a way that makes it appear legitimate. When user clicks on the link, they may be directed to a harmful website or prompted to download malicious files.



• Frame Injection – This attack involved embedding a webpage within an invisible frame on another site, User interacts with what appears to be a legitimate site, but their actions are performed on the malicious page, potentially leading to unintended actions or data theft.

z_impl_pwm_capture_cycles() in drivers/pwm/pwm_capture.c stores its capture context (struct z_pwm_capture_cb_data, including a struct k_sem) on its own stack and registers a pointer to it as the driver capture callback's user_data. When called with a K_NO_WAIT timeout, k_sem_take() returns -EBUSY, which the function did not handle: it fell through, returned the uninitialized status field, copied uninitialized period/pulse values to the caller when that status happened to be zero, and returned without disabling the capture or clearing the callback.

pwm_capture_cycles() is a system call, and z_vrfy_pwm_capture_cycles() passes the caller's timeout through unchanged. With CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_PWM_CAPTURE enabled, an unprivileged user-mode thread that has been granted access to a capture-capable PWM device can pass K_NO_WAIT to trigger the defect. Without userspace the function is only reachable from trusted application code.

The uninitialized values come from the thread's privileged (kernel) stack, so a user-mode caller can read up to 8 bytes of stale kernel stack memory per call. More seriously, when the capture later completes, the driver ISR invokes z_pwm_capture_cycles_callback() with the dangling pointer. The callback writes into the expired kernel stack region and calls k_sem_give() on whatever memory now occupies it, which can corrupt live kernel stack frames and make the scheduler walk a forged wait queue. The result is kernel memory corruption from interrupt context, leading at least to a crash and possibly to privilege escalation out of the userspace sandbox. The fix rejects K_NO_WAIT with -EINVAL before any capture is configured.

The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) points drv_data->rx_buf.data at an rx_packet buffer on the caller's stack and enables the UART RX interrupt before waiting 1500 ms for a reply. When the wait timed out, transceive_packet() returned -ETIMEDOUT but left the RX interrupt enabled and rx_buf.data still pointing at the caller's buffer.

Once the caller's frame has returned, any bytes that arrive late on the UART are written by the interrupt handler uart_cb_handler() through the dangling pointer into stack memory that the thread has since reused. The bytes come from the device on the other end of the UART. An attacker with physical access who replaces or impersonates the fingerprint module can trigger this by delaying a reply past the timeout and then sending a packet. A slow or faulty genuine module can also trigger it by accident.

The result is a write of attacker-chosen bytes into a live thread stack. The write length comes from the header of the late packet. Commit 96968fac22b, which landed together with this fix, bounds it to a header plus CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE bytes; affected releases do not have that bound. This can crash the device and may allow control-flow hijacking, depending on what occupies the reused stack region. The fix disables the RX interrupt, resets the RX semaphore and clears rx_buf.data on timeout, and the interrupt handler now refuses to write when no receive buffer is armed.

The Grow R502-A fingerprint sensor driver (drivers/sensor/grow_r502a/grow_r502a.c) receives sensor responses in the UART interrupt handler uart_cb_handler(). Once the 9-byte header has arrived, the handler reads the 16-bit package length from the header and uses it as the byte count for further uart_fifo_read() calls into rx_buf.data. It never checks that length against the destination buffer. That buffer is a union r502a_packet on the calling thread's stack, set up by transceive_packet(), and is only CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE + 12 bytes long (140 bytes by default).

A malicious or counterfeit sensor module, or an attacker who tampers with the UART wiring, can reply to any driver command with a header that declares a length of up to 65535 bytes. The ISR then writes that many attacker-supplied bytes past the end of the stack buffer. The existing length check in r502a_validate_rx_packet() runs only after the data has been written, so it does not prevent the overflow. Every sensor transaction is affected, including the ones issued by fps_init() during device initialization.

The result is a stack overwrite with attacker-controlled length and content in the calling thread. This can corrupt control data and may lead to arbitrary code execution on the host MCU, which would undermine any function the fingerprint sensor is meant to protect. The fix validates the declared length against CONFIG_R502A_DATA_PKT_SIZE as soon as the header is complete and aborts the reception if it is out of range.

This is due to the `LoginGoogle::login()` function failing to validate the `aud` (audience) claim of the supplied `idToken` against any OAuth client ID belonging to the WordPress site, failing to verify the `email_verified` claim, and resolving WordPress accounts solely by the email claim without binding to the Google `sub` (subject) identifier — while the `/app-builder/v1/login` REST endpoint is registered with a `permission_callback` that unconditionally returns `true`, leaving it fully reachable by unauthenticated requesters. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as any existing WordPress user — including Administrators — whose email address is known, by supplying a Google-signed ID token obtained from an entirely unrelated OAuth client containing the target user's email claim, which causes the plugin to issue a signed App Builder JWT granting that user's full privileges. Exploitation requires the attacker to obtain a valid Google-signed ID token carrying the target user's email address, which can be achieved by operating a separate Google OAuth client and inducing the target user to authenticate through it.
Rejected reason: This CVE ID has been rejected or withdrawn by its CVE Numbering Authority.

The Product Input Fields for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0 via the process_file_input_field function. This is due to missing file type validation in the process_file_input_field function, which accepts the client-supplied multipart Content-Type header as the sole type gate and writes the uploaded file to the unprotected pif_temp directory using the verbatim client-supplied filename. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one product with a File-type Product Input Field with the "Show thumbnail" option enabled, which is a standard use of the feature; additionally, the pif_temp/ upload directory is created without .htaccess or index.php restrictions, leaving written files directly web-accessible and executable on default Apache/mod_php configurations.

In Eclipse Che versions 7.61.0 through 7.124.0 three related defects in the SCM-OAuth flow, chain into a Medium-severity finding:



1. Open redirect (CWE-601) — `EmbeddedOAuthAPI.callback()` and the OAuth1 callback issue `307 Temporary Redirect` to whatever URL was carried in the `redirect_after_login` field of the OAuth `state` parameter. The value is fully attacker-controlled and never compared against an allow-list of permitted hosts.



2. Missing CSRF nonce in OAuth `state` (CWE-352) — `OAuthAuthenticator.prepareState()` builds the `state` parameter solely by URL-encoding the original request's query string. No random nonce is bound to the user's session, so an attacker can pre-compute a callback URL carrying _their own_ SCM authorization `code` and have a logged-in victim open it. `callback()` then stores the attacker's SCM token under the victim's Che identity (`personalAccessTokenManager.store(...)`).



3. Mutable field on a `@Singleton` (CWE-362 / CWE-488) — `EmbeddedOAuthAPI` is `@Singleton` but stores the per-request `redirect_after_login` value into the instance field `private String redirectAfterLogin`. Any user's `authenticate()` call overwrites the field for all concurrent users; the `access_denied` error-path of `callback()` then redirects to the _last writer's_ URL.

File Permission Vulnerability in RV3000 Log Monitor for VMware.

This issue affects RV3000 Log Monitor for VMware(CIM): before 98-09; RV3000 Log Monitor for VMware: before 97-05.

The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. The handler sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content_callback() is registered on the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call_user_func() after only a function_exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.

A Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in the eventbus execution in Google Cloud Application Integration versions prior to 2026-09-22 on Google Cloud Platform allows an authenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution using a crafted serialized Java object.


This vulnerability was patched on 22 September 2026, and no customer action is needed.

EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition contains an OS command injection vulnerability which may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary OS commands with root or SYSTEM privileges on the system running the affected product.

GNU m4 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in reload_frozen_state() in src/freeze.c. When processing a malicious frozen-state file via the -R option, an attacker can trigger an oversized allocation request that crashes the program, causing denial of service.


This issue was fixed in commit 69aef802fb25ab600d37210f44e5128633cbc432.

The WebP Express plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.25.15 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the WebP Express "URL replacement" method is set to "Alter HTML", and full privilege escalation — such as provisioning a new administrator account — requires a logged-in administrator to view the frontend page on which the injected comment is rendered.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.11 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with developer-role permissions to self-approve their own merge request and merge code into protected branches due to incorrect authorization when a security policy prohibited author self-approval.

The Fluent Forms – Customizable Contact Forms, Survey, Quiz, & Conversational Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Pre-Hijacking via Unverified Identifier in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.15. The vulnerability exists because the `PaymentHandler::maybeAssignTransactions()` function, registered on the `user_register` hook at priority 99, resolves the lookup email solely from the newly created user record via the `user_email` parameter with no prior verification that the registrant actually controls that address, then bulk-updates all guest transactions and submissions in `wp_fluentform_transactions` and `wp_fluentform_submissions` whose `payer_email` matches and whose `user_id` is NULL to assign ownership to the attacker's new account. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to pre-hijack a victim's prior guest payment history — reading their payment receipts and cancelling their active subscriptions via the `[fluentform_payments]` shortcode and the `wp_ajax_fluentform_user_payment_endpoints` `cancel_transaction` route — by simply registering an account under the victim's email address before the legitimate owner does. Exploitation requires that the WordPress site has open user registration enabled and that the targeted victim previously submitted at least one payment as a guest under their email address.

The SlimStat Analytics plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'filter_array' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a non-default administrator configuration in which the can_view whitelist contains at least one username of which the attacker's login is a substring (e.g., can_view set to 'trustedreporter' while the attacker's login is 'report'), and the stored payload only fires when an administrator subsequently opens the Saved Filters dialog.

The WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 via the `REQUEST_URI` query parameter. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in `showLoginForm()`: the plugin's `isRestUrl()` function performs an unanchored `strpos()` prefix match against the full `REQUEST_URI` — including the query string — and short-circuits all authorization checks (including `isStagingSite()` and `current_user_can('manage_options')`) whenever it detects a REST-like URL, while WordPress core only treats a request as a REST API call when the `rest_route` query variable is non-empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to bypass the staging-site login gate entirely by appending an empty `rest_route` parameter (e.g. `/wp-json/?rest_route=`), causing the plugin to skip its gate while core proceeds to render the ordinary theme front end, exposing the full theme-rendered contents of the staging site — including private post content, page-builder output, WooCommerce pages, and site search results over the staging database. This bypass only affects staging sites where the login gate is active, which is the default state for any site cloned by the plugin when the `wpstg_is_staging_site` option is set to `true` or the `.wp-staging` marker file is present in `ABSPATH`.

Authentication bypass in the system.setPillar and system.getPillar functions in Uyuni before 5.1.35, 5.2.0 before 5.2.25, 5.3.0 before 5.3.5 could be used by logged in attackers to inject code into other managed system spaces.

The LA-Studio Element Kit for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.3 via the 'actions[*][data][autocomplete][query][fields] (and [get_titles][query][fields])' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to extract sensitive user data including password hashes (user_pass), email addresses, and activation keys for all registered accounts including administrators. The elementor_ajax nonce used as the sole access control is available to any logged-in user via the globally exposed elementorCommonConfig JavaScript object, making both AJAX actions trivially reachable at Subscriber privilege level.

Stack-based buffer overflow in the mkevent helper in Checkmk <2.5.0p21, <2.4.0p42 and 2.3.0 (EOL) allows an attacker who controls the check output of a monitored host to crash mkevent, causing the notification to be lost, or to redirect the notification to an IPv4 address of their choice, if notifications are forwarded to the Event Console.

Chainlit is vulnerable to a file upload block bypass in the "spontaneous_file_upload" functionality. Disabling the feature with the "enabled = false" option only affects the frontend, while the backend upload endpoints remain active and can be abused directly. An attacker with a valid session ID can send requests to these backend endpoints to upload arbitrary file types and then generate a retrieval URL that is accessible to anyone who obtains the link. This allows the attacker to serve malicious content, such as a fake login pages, from the application's trusted domain, which can be used for phishing attacks against users.




The vulnerability has only been confirmed in versions 2.10.0 and 2.12.0 but may also affect other versions.

The EWWW Image Optimizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.9.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core comment kses permits the payload's tag and attribute structure unchanged at save time, meaning the malicious content bypasses save-time sanitization and is only activated when the plugin's output-buffer filter processes the page on render.

The Postie plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.89 via the 'postie' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract the plaintext POP3/IMAP mailbox password and username, SMTP configuration, absolute server filesystem paths, and all SQL queries executed during the mail-fetch run from the debug response body. Exploitation requires the site administrator to have enabled the 'Enable Debug Logging' (postie_log_debug) option, which is off by default but is routinely toggled on during troubleshooting and left enabled.
Rejected reason: CVE-2026-110928 has been marked as a duplicate of CVE-2026-106586.

Siemens Software Center contains an uncontrolled search path element vulnerability that could allow an authenticated local attacker to place a specially crafted DLL in a directory that the application searches, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the affected application.

The Smaily Connect plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 3.24.0 This is due to the smaily_get_edit_user_id() function reading an attacker-controlled $_GET['user_id'] parameter without performing any ownership or capability check, and then feeding that id into smaily_get_userdata() (which calls get_user_meta()) when rendering the WooCommerce My Account 'edit-account' form via the smaily_print_user_frontend_fields() handler on the woocommerce_edit_account_form action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to read other users' personally identifiable profile data (phone number, date of birth, and gender — including administrators') by appending ?user_id=<target> to the account-details URL.

The Email Encoder – Protect Email Addresses and Phone Numbers plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a site administrator to have enabled the plugin's non-default "Protect custom href attributes" setting (e.g. configured to 'tel'), and injected comments must pass standard WordPress moderation before the script executes for visiting users.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in WPExperts NOWPayments for WooCommerce nowpayments-for-woocommerce allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects NOWPayments for WooCommerce: from n/a through 1.4.1.

A path traversal vulnerability in Medusa’s product import functionality, specifically in the handling of the 'file_key' parameter of the '/admin/products/imports' endpoint. The lack of proper validation allows an authenticated remote attacker with administrative access to reference system files outside the intended import directory. When attempting to process these files as CSV files, the application may partially reveal their contents through parsing or validation error messages. Additionally, cleanup routines operate on paths controlled by the attacker, which could allow the deletion of files accessible to the application process and affect system availability.

The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The phsuperpack module for PrestaShop is vulnerable to a missing authorization check. The controller at /module/phsuperpack/pack can be accessed without login, which allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to modify the module's data and create, edit, or delete products, including the complete deletion of a product with its translations, shop associations, stock, and images.



This issue was fixed in version 3.0.26.

The phsuperpack module for PrestaShop is vulnerable to SQL injection in the /module/phsuperpack/pack endpoint. User-supplied input is used in database queries without proper sanitization. An authenticated, high privileged, remote attacker can exploit this by sending crafted input to read or modify data in the shop's database. Critically, because of CVE-2026-114346, this endpoint may be accessed without authentication.



This issue was fixed in version 3.0.26.

Path traversal in TPM device management in Canonical LXD from 4.8 before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a remote authenticated user with project access to recursively delete arbitrary files and directories on the host as root via a crafted device name during instance or device removal.

LightRAG provides simple and fast retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 1.5.5, query responses are cached under a key that omits conversation_history, so an unauthenticated attacker can poison the cached answers returned to other users who send the same query. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.5.

The Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 7.4.0 does not perform authorisation checks when rendering its front-end print document for a reserved order identifier, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the configured store contact details (including the site administrator's email address) and to create Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 7.4.0 files in arbitrary existing, writable directories outside the Print Invoice & Delivery Notes for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 7.4.0's own folder.

The User Registration & Membership – Free & Paid Memberships, Subscriptions, Content Restriction, User Profile, Custom User Registration & Login Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_data (field_name=user_registration_description)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the active theme to render the_archive_description() on the author archive template, as is the case with Hello Elementor, Kadence, GeneratePress, Twenty Sixteen, Storefront, and other common themes.

NetBird is a zero-trust networking platform that connects people, machines, and AI agents across any network. From versions 0.5.0 through 0.75.1, the client daemon exposes its gRPC control interface to any local process without authentication. On Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD, the interface is a Unix domain socket that is accessible to all local users, allowing any of them to control the daemon. An attacker with a low-privilege account can read or modify privileged VPN and daemon settings, disconnect or hijack the NetBird peer, and gain an unauthenticated root shell via the built-in SSH server. This issue is fixed in version 0.76.0.
In affected versions of Octopus Server, authenticated users without permissions to perform write actions on specific endpoints are able to do so due to insufficient permission validation
Rejected reason: Not a separate vulnerability: dependency update. See GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. Display and Debug formatting of User IDs and notation data does not escape control characters. When an application prints those values, a crafted User ID or notation can misrender the identity or alter terminal output.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The ASCII-armor reader does not limit the length of a line. Parsing an armored message with a very long line can exhaust memory in the process. Memory use follows the input size, with a small constant factor, and is not a classic amplification.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The default ASCII-armor parser accepts Unicode dash characters in armor framing and ignores leading quote characters. A crafted byte stream can be parsed as one message by this tolerant parser and as a different message by a strict ASCII-armor parser. The strict mode is opt-in; the default parser remains tolerant.

A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. DSA signature verification does not reject a public key with generator 1 and public value 1 before calling the cryptographic backend. Upstream reports that the Nettle and OpenSSL backends, including the default Nettle build, accept this key. Under that key, a signature can verify for every message. Ordinary DSA keys are not affected. An application is exposed when that degenerate certificate is accepted as authoritative.

In LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2, an improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to write and delete files at arbitrary host filesystem paths as root.

 When a custom storage volume is pushed to a LXD daemon, the snapshot names supplied by the migration peer are never validated and are used to build the filesystem path of each received snapshot. This allows an attacker to place attacker-controlled files into any host directory as root, gaining root-level code execution on the host, and to recursively delete an attacker-chosen path.

In LXD before 5.21.0 and 6.10.0, an OS command injection vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to execute arbitrary code as root on the host.

 The raw.dnsmasq bridge network configuration key is not restricted to server administrators and is copied verbatim into the dnsmasq configuration file, so a user whose project keeps the default features.networks=false can have a bridge network created in the default project with an injected dhcp-script directive. This allows an attacker to make the host dnsmasq execute attacker-chosen code as root on a DHCP lease event and fully compromise the host.

The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy_files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy_files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in WPTasty Business Directory business-directory-plugin allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Business Directory: from n/a through 6.4.29.

Google Chromium V8 out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.

The Forminator Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Approval Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.3 via the forminator_replace_custom_form_data() function. This is due to the function expanding the {all_fields} merge tag before {account_approval_link}, so a submitter-supplied field value containing the literal string {account_approval_link} is resolved into the real activation URL, including the secret activation key, in the user confirmation email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain the activation link for their own pending registration and activate the account via the ?page=account_activation&key= endpoint, bypassing the manual approval configured on the registration form. Exploitation requires a user-registration form with manual approval enabled and a user confirmation email that includes the {all_fields} merge tag (the default template). Note: On WordPress Multisite installations with site registration enabled, the self-activated account also becomes the Administrator of the subsite created during registration.

The VK Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.130.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the moderator to interact with the inline Reply action on the edit-comments screen, which is a routine action triggered when a moderation-held comment is reviewed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

NocoDB is software for building databases as spreadsheets. Prior to 2026.08.0, the row-scoped endpoints of a public shared view check whether a target record exists by primary key without applying the view's row filter, while the view's list and count endpoints do apply it. A recipient of a shared-view link, including its password where one is configured, can list the linked records of a filtered-out record and obtain signed download paths for its attachments by guessing its primary key. This issue is fixed in version 2026.08.0.

The WP Photo Album Plus plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upn-name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.3.06.002 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's Frontend Edit feature to be enabled by the site administrator, which allows photo owners to update photo names via the update-photo-new REST endpoint.

The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'price_disabled_msg' setting in versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 The uni_cpo_save_settings_data() AJAX handler applies html_entity_decode() to the output of uni_cpo_sanitize_text(), which itself already runs html_entity_decode() before wp_kses(); this double decode allows a double-entity-encoded tag to pass wp_kses as inert text and then be re-materialised as live HTML before being stored in the _cpo_price_disabled_msg post meta and later echoed via do_shortcode() on the single-product page without further escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Shop Manager-level access (edit_products) and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected product page.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Drupal Content Synchronizer allows Object Injection. This issue affects Content Synchronizer versions: from 0.0.0 to 4.1.1.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Content Synchronizer allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects Content Synchronizer versions: from 0.0.0 to 4.1.1.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in lasp-lang partisan allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to abort the Erlang VM of a node via Excessive Allocation. partisan_peer_service_server:handle_info/2 decodes every frame that arrives on the peer listener with binary_to_term/1, without the safe option, before handle_inbound/2 interprets the message and before any peer authentication takes place. TLS is off by default and the listener accepts connections from any host, so one frame that names more atoms than the atom table holds aborts the VM. partisan_peer_service_client:handle_info/2 decodes frames from the server side of a connection the same way.

The decode also materializes funs, ports and references the frame encodes and inflates compressed terms. The demonstrated impact is denial of service. partisan does not invoke decoded funs, so code execution was not shown.

This issue affects partisan: from 3.0.0 before 6.4.0.

The Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based blind SQL Injection via the 'instance[lists]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The wpmlgetlistfields AJAX handler performs only a nonce check with no capability check, and the required refreshfields nonce is emitted on every wp-admin page including /wp-admin/profile.php, making the endpoint trivially reachable by any authenticated Subscriber.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the `ajax_revert()` AJAX handler. The vulnerability exists because the `remove_optimizations()` function reads attacker-controlled values from the unprotected `w3tc_imageservice` post meta key — which carries no underscore prefix and no registered authorization callback, making it writable by any user with `edit_post` capability via WordPress's built-in custom-fields AJAX endpoint — and passes those values directly to `wp_delete_attachment()` with no check that the referenced ID is a child of the caller's own post, is an actual attachment, or that the caller holds `delete_post` capability on it. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Author-level access or above to permanently delete any WordPress attachment in the media library, including media files owned by other users along with their associated files on disk, regardless of ownership — a capability not available through the normal WordPress interface. The revert nonce is exposed via `wp_localize_script` on `/wp-admin/upload.php` to any user with `upload_files` capability, ensuring the nonce check that is present does not serve as a meaningful barrier to Author-level exploitation.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via the 'utm_source (and the wp-resetpass-<hash> cookie on the victim side)' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract the live password-reset key (rp_key) embedded in the cached reset form, enabling full account takeover of the targeted administrator. Exploitation requires the page-cache engine to be configured as Disk: Basic, Memcached, Redis, or APC with the 'Cache URI with query string variables' option enabled, and the victim must visit an attacker-crafted URL containing utm_source=wp-locations.php while their wp-resetpass cookie remains active.

The Points Management System For Gamification, Ranks, Badges, and Loyalty Rewards Program – myCred plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'key' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the Link Clicks hook to be enabled and that the attacker, as a Subscriber-level user, can access any front-end page rendering the [mycred_link] shortcode, which localizes the nonce needed to reach the AJAX endpoint.

The Swift Performance Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI (gated by $_GET['force-cache'])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.7.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is planted via a single unauthenticated GET request to any URL with ?force-cache=1 and a URL-encoded HTML payload in the path, which the plugin decodes and creates as a literal filesystem directory name; the script fires the next time an administrator opens the Swift Performance dashboard.

The Hide My WP Ghost – Security & Firewall plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.0.15 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the plugin's URL rewriting mode is active (hmwp_mode set to a non-default value) and that the attacker has one previously approved comment from the same author/email address, after which WordPress auto-approves the attack comment without moderator intervention.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to obtain another user's authenticated session cookie and gain unauthorized access to that user's account due to improper session storage handling in the dependency proxy authentication flow when a redirect-pending state was triggered.

The Timetics – Appointment Booking Calendar & Scheduling System plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data and user account creation in versions up to, and including, 1.0.67 This is due to the public `POST /wp-json/timetics/v1/bookings` route being registered with `permission_callback => function () { return true; }` and the handler (`create_item()` → `save_bookings()` → `booking_appointment()`) passing the attacker-controlled `email` directly into `Customer::make()`, which (a) grants the `timetics-customer` role to any existing WordPress user matched by email — including administrators and staff — and overwrites that account's `first_name`/`last_name` user meta, and (b) calls `wp_insert_user()` with role `timetics-customer` when the email is new, regardless of the site's `users_can_register` setting. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to create arbitrary WordPress user accounts, assign the `timetics-customer` role to existing accounts (including administrators), and overwrite their profile metadata.

The Duplicate Post plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[custom][names][prefix]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the site owner to have enabled both 'User Level Permissions' for the Subscriber role and the 'Show reference to original item?' option, and the targeted administrator must view the edit screen of the chained copy post in the classic editor.

The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'post_field_conditions[0][field]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The vulnerability requires a two-step exploit: a crafted field value must first be stored via the wp_ajax_automatorwp_update_item_option AJAX endpoint, and then the target automation must be triggered to fire the vulnerable SQL query.

The Apache Airflow TaskFlow decorators @task.bash, @task.sql, @task.analytics, @task.kubernetes_cmd and the common.ai decorators (@task.llm, @task.agent, @task.llm_sql, @task.llm_branch, @task.llm_file_analysis, @task.llm_schema_compare) rendered Jinja templates a second time after the task runner had already rendered them, so any value copied into env, op_args, op_kwargs or the returned prompt, command or SQL was evaluated as a template on the worker. An attacker who can only trigger a Dag run (for example a user with trigger permission supplying run conf), or who controls text that a Dag passes into one of these decorators as an argument or prompt (for example a ticket or a downloaded document), could run arbitrary commands on the worker and read connection passwords and Variables, in any deployment that uses an affected decorator in a Dag that passes such input through env, parameters or prompt. Users are recommended to upgrade apache-airflow-providers-standard to 1.22.0, apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes to 11.0.0, apache-airflow-providers-common-sql to 3.0.0 and apache-airflow-providers-common-ai to 1.2.0 or later.

The Widgets for Social Photo Feed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'widget-id' shortcode attribute of the [trustindex-feed] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 1.8.3 This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping in the registerWidget() function, which concatenates the raw shortcode attribute directly into a double-quoted JavaScript string literal that is then enqueued via wp_add_inline_script() and rendered in wp_footer/admin_footer. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (via wp-admin/post.php add_meta → post_meta key 'my_field')' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor can store a raw script payload in a custom field on their own draft and cause it to execute in an administrator's or editor's authenticated browser session when they preview or publish the post.

The Enfold theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'templateName' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The AJAX save handler validates a nonce and requires only the edit_posts capability, meaning a Contributor can legitimately obtain the nonce from their own post-edit screen and store a malicious template name that subsequently fires in every privileged user's session.

The Maps Plugin using Google Maps for WordPress - WP Google Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the array keys of the `categories` entries parsed from an imported JSON file in versions up to, and including, 1.9.9 This is due to the wgm_handle_import() function sanitizing only the known-named VALUES (`name`, `icon`) of each category object while passing the attacker-controlled JSON object KEYS directly to `$wpdb->insert()`, which interpolates them as column names into the generated INSERT statement without escaping embedded backticks. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above (when the plugin's own 'Minimum Role for Map Editor' setting has been configured to 'Subscriber', one of five values the plugin's settings UI offers), to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database, including administrator password hashes.

The MW WP Form plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 5.1.8 via the 'mw-wp-form_session_mw-wp-form-<FORM_ID>' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite or delete arbitrary WordPress transients in wp_options — including core-managed transients such as wp_styles_for_blocks — enabling injection of attacker-controlled CSS into every front-end page and permanent anchoring of poisoned transient values that never re-expire. The plugin's CSRF check does not prevent exploitation because MW_WP_Form_Data::__construct() registers _save_to_session() on the PHP shutdown hook before the CSRF check runs, causing the transient write to fire even after wp_safe_redirect()+exit; the GET path via the [mwform_formkey] shortcode has no CSRF check at all.

The Postie plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'email HTML body' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.91 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable when the processing request runs under a user holding the unfiltered_html capability — either because 'Force User Login' is enabled and Postie switches to the default poster, or because an administrator manually triggers the fetch — causing wp_filter_post_kses to be stripped from content_save_pre and the attribute-breakout markup to be stored verbatim by wp_insert_post().

The Co-Authors, Multiple Authors and Guest Authors in an Author Box with PublishPress Authors plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'nickname' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.20.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is possible because sanitize_text_field() passes entity-encoded sequences such as < and > through unchanged, allowing a Subscriber to store a breakout payload in their WordPress nickname that is later decoded into live HTML markup by wp_localize_script() and injected into the DOM via jQuery's replaceWith().

The Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'dfile (any CF7 file field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.5.58 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful script execution additionally requires a web server that returns no explicit Content-Type header for the targeted audio/video extension, causing the browser to sniff and render the uploaded file as text/html; default Apache configurations without mod_headers or without honoring .htaccess satisfy this condition. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The User Registration & Membership – Free & Paid Memberships, Subscriptions, Content Restriction, User Profile, Custom User Registration & Login Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'user_registration_<checkbox_field_name>[]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The self-registration endpoint (wp_ajax_nopriv_user_registration_user_form_submit) requires no nonce, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to create a Subscriber account and then supply the malicious checkbox value through the authenticated profile-update action using a legitimately obtained nonce.

Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

The SlimStat Analytics – Real-Time Stats, Heatmaps & Ecommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the non-default 'Show user agent' (slimstat_options[show_complete_user_agent_tooltip]) setting to be enabled, which causes the raw stored User-Agent value to be used as the tooltip title instead of a sanitized browser name.

Kestra is an open-source control plane for workflows across data, infrastructure, and applications. Prior to version 2.0.1, the namespace-files export endpoint places an unvalidated namespace path segment into the Content-Disposition filename of the ZIP download. An attacker who tricks a user into following a crafted export URL can inject Content-Disposition header parameters to spoof the saved filename or extension. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.1.

The Beautiful taxonomy filters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'term_name (reflected from DB)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an attacker to first create a maliciously-named taxonomy term as an Author-level user; the nonce required to trigger execution is publicly emitted on any front-end page displaying the taxonomy filter widget, making the injected payload reachable by completely unauthenticated visitors.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Planet Pay Planet Pay payments planet-pay-payment allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Planet Pay payments: from n/a through 5.4.4.

The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_text (shortcode attribute of [vc_cta])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The style="classic" shortcode attribute must be used to trigger the vulnerable code path that feeds custom_text through vc_get_css_color into the inline style attribute; wp_kses_post applied at save time does not neutralize the payload because the attacker's value contains no HTML tags, only a double quote inside a shortcode attribute, leaving the injected content intact in post_content.
Rejected reason: this CVE was issued in error.

An improper access control vulnerability exists in a privileged Unix domain socket of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). Due to insufficient authorization checks, a low-privileged local attacker can interact with the daemon and invoke privileged operations without the necessary permissions. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the firmware update functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with admin privileges can upload a crafted firmware package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the system. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An HTML injection vulnerability exists in the alert notification functionality of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of agent-supplied data. An attacker controlling an agent identity can submit crafted HTML content, potentially allowing the attacker to manipulate displayed content or deceive recipients. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the update functionality of StellarOne due to insufficient validation of files contained within uploaded update packages. An attacker with web administrator privileges can upload a crafted update package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in an Accounts Manager service of StellarOne running inside a container due to improper handling of user-supplied input in SQL queries. An attacker with command execution access to the host system or another container with network connectivity to the affected service can send crafted requests to manipulate backend database queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper version validation vulnerability exists in the product update mechanism of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). An attacker with product admin privileges can downgrade the product to an older, potentially vulnerable version, potentially allowing previously patched vulnerabilities to be reintroduced and security protections to be weakened. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the patch apply functionality of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux) due to insufficient validation of uploaded patch packages before extraction. An attacker with low-privileged web access can upload a crafted patch package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the vShell command-line interface of StellarOne due to improper validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with access to vShell can inject crafted commands to bypass the restricted shell environment and execute arbitrary operating system commands. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An arbitrary file write vulnerability exists in the patch upload functionality of StellarOne due to improper validation of file paths. An attacker with admin web access can upload a crafted patch package to write arbitrary files on endpoints with the privileges of the endpoint service. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the patch management functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with Viewer web access can perform administrative patch management operations. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the Search Agents API of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with Viewer privileges can send crafted requests to manipulate backend SQL queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.
An out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Qt VectorImage component of the Qt Quick module.

An attacker allowed to send AXFR or IXFR queries can cause an outgoing TCP connection to the backend to be stuck, causing a denial of service to other clients trying to reuse the same outgoing connection.
An attacker can cause a denial of service by sending crafted HTTP queries to the internal webserver. The webserver is not enabled by default and is protected by an ACL.

Missing authorization in the page behind the "Changes" slideout of the main menu in Checkmk versions 2.5.0 before 2.5.0p20 allows any authenticated user, including users with the built-in "Guest user" role, to read the text, author and time of all pending changes and the version, online status, login status and last activation result of all sites.

The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'position' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is stored via the unauthenticated wp_ajax_nopriv_ ESSB stat log AJAX action, which performs no nonce or capability check, and executes when the attacker-controlled position value is rendered verbatim into a double-quoted HTML data-* attribute where the unescaped quote allows attribute breakout.

In authd before 0.7.2, an improper access control vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to complete a first-time SSH login with another account's UID and incorrect primary GID, and to read or modify files owned by that account. This allows an attacker to access another account's data, potentially enabling account takeover or privilege escalation.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 inserts message-derived values into LDAP filters used by the ldap_compare and ldap_read mail-rule operations without LDAP filter escaping. An unauthenticated remote sender can alter an LDAP-backed rule query when a deployed rule uses attacker-controlled message data, potentially changing policy decisions or exposing data returned to later rule processing.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 copies an insufficiently sanitized DKIM identity into authentication results and may preserve the injected result in an ARC seal. An unauthenticated remote sender can create misleading authentication claims that downstream systems may trust when DKIM verification and ARC sealing are enabled.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 exposes an unauthenticated, world-writable local configuration socket whose root daemon accepts shell commands. An attacker with local low-privilege code execution can execute arbitrary commands as root and take complete control of the appliance.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 interpolates a stored GINA account address into a root boot-job shell command without neutralization. An authenticated internal attacker who can prepare the required account state, arrange for the migration marker to be absent, and cause a reboot can execute arbitrary commands as root.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 reuses a broad legacy GINA session purpose across registration and recovery workflows. A remote attacker who knows an account security answer can use a recovery session in a different account workflow to replace credentials and account recovery data, and may delete the account when self-deletion is enabled.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 permits LDAP wildcard characters in legacy GINA identifiers and inserts those values into account, token, certificate, and key lookup filters without escaping. An unauthenticated remote attacker can alter which directory entry is selected and may disclose account existence or cause later workflow logic to use an unintended entry.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 exposes legacy GINA password-reset paths that can replace a registered account credential without authenticating the requester. A remote attacker who knows the account address can force a reset when a configured administrator or valid stored creator is present, disrupting access and revoking active API tokens; the replacement credential is sent only to a pre-existing trusted recipient.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 uses a source-visible hard-coded fallback secret for legacy GINA token and Large File Transfer cryptographic operations when expected key material is unavailable or unusable. A remote attacker can forge accepted account tokens while the fallback path is active and can decrypt LFT content protected with the shared fallback.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 writes legacy GINA multipart uploads before authenticating the caller and does not remove files created by failed or unauthenticated requests. An unauthenticated remote attacker can accumulate persistent upload files and exhaust the backing filesystem, disrupting GINA and other services sharing that storage.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 normalizes hyphenated and underscore forms of a trusted GINA routing header to the same backend variable. A remote attacker can create a merged invalid selector that makes legacy GINA and GINAv2 fall back to the default domain policy, potentially crossing tenant or policy boundaries in multi-domain deployments.

The NextMove Lite – Thank You Page for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.email' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.24.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script fires without any victim interaction because the builder page's JavaScript calls $(".preview_order_id").trigger("change") on page load, immediately executing any attribute-injected event handler.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-1' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution is not automatic on page load; the injected script runs only when an administrator actively clicks the stored ThickBox link, at which point WordPress ThickBox JS decodes the entity-encoded title attribute and writes it into #TB_ajaxWindowTitle via innerHTML in the administrator's origin. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The WPMR Google Feed Manager for WooCommerce – Sell on Google Merchant Center & Shopping plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'feed (title field inside the JSON-encoded feed array)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.24.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. sanitize_text_field() is applied on storage but strips only angle brackets and newlines, leaving single quotes and parentheses intact — the exact characters needed to break out of the onclick JavaScript string context constructed by wppfm_feedListTable() and installed via jQuery .append().

A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the vlv_value_compare() function in vlv_pagination.c of the Virtual List View module in the **Samba** package. The function uses the sort value from the search result with no check that the result still contains that attribute. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can search the directory sends a Virtual List View search by value, sorted on an attribute the matching entries do not have. The LDAP worker that handles the search exits, which disconnects the directory clients that were using that worker, and the directory service starts a replacement worker. Another search of the same kind crashes the worker that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that worker is replaced, so repeating the search keeps the LDAP service from staying available. The same crash follows a search sorted on an attribute the attacker is not allowed to read. The directory removes that attribute from the result, and the comparison uses the missing value.

A **Type Confusion** has been found in the dns_to_dnsp_convert() function in dnsdata.c of the DNS server RPC module in the **Samba** package. The function copies an HINFO record from the management request into the stored DNS record without converting the request name into the two strings the stored record uses. A low-privileged network attacker or user in the DnsAdmins group adds an HINFO record through the DNS management interface. The directory process that handles the add also serves the directory's other remote calls. That process exits, which disconnects the clients that were using it, and the directory service starts a replacement process. Another add of the same kind crashes the process that accepts it, and each further crash waits longer before that process is replaced, so repeating the add keeps the directory remote-call service from staying available.

A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the acl_check_dns_host_name() and acl_validate_spn_value() functions in source4/dsdb/samdb/ldb_modules/acl.c of the Active Directory domain controller ACL module in the **Samba** package. The checks read the account name after a request that removes it, and they do not test that the value is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can update the DNS host name or service principal name of their own computer account can include a removal of sAMAccountName in that same LDAP modify. The directory process crashes. Repeating the modify keeps the directory service unavailable.

The Funnelforms Free – Multi Step Form, Contact Form & Lead Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'document.settings.heading' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. Docker Sandboxes re-resolves saved mount paths when replacing a sandbox container during kit changes or restarting a sandbox. An attacker able to replace a source ancestor in a shared writable workspace with a symlink can redirect another sandbox's mount to a different host directory, exposing its contents and permitting modification through read-write mounts. The destination must remain accessible to the daemon and allowed by policy where enforced. Saved-mount replay during kit replacement was introduced in version 0.35.0; ordinary restart replay was added in version 0.45.0. This saved-mount replay issue is fixed in version 0.54.0.

The WPForms (Contact Form by WPForms / wpforms-lite) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the Multiple Choice field's 'Other' option value on payment forms in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a privileged user such as an administrator accesses the injected payment entry on the WPForms > Payments details page. The submitted value is stored via sanitize_text_field(), which preserves a space-separated pseudo-tag (e.g. '< i class="wpforms-single-payment-tooltip" data-tooltip-content="<img src=x onerror=...>">x< /i>') because strip_tags() ignores a '<' followed by whitespace; on the admin Payments entry page the value is output through wp_kses() with the 'post' allowlist, which normalizes it into a live <i> element retaining its class and data-* attributes, and the bundled Tooltipster initialization (contentAsHTML + contentCloning) then renders the attribute's HTML, executing the script on page load without any hover.

A **server-side request forgery** flaw has been found in the get_remote_artifact_url() function in pulp_python/app/models.py of the pull-through caching feature in the **pulp_python** package. The function uses the redirect query parameter from the client request as the URL to download. A network attacker or user who can reach the content app of a Python distribution that has a remote can choose that URL. The content app downloads it and returns the response. When the remote has a username and password, the download sends those credentials to the host in the URL. When the remote policy is immediate, the default, or on_demand, the file is saved into the distribution's repository and later clients are served that file. The project name and version come from the file, and the filename comes from the request path. A filename the repository already stores is served from the stored file.

Bizum Pay for Android incorporates static values within the APK to authenticate and sign requests to its API, including those for user registration. These values are common across different installations and can be extracted from the APK. An attacker who obtains the application could reuse them to generate requests that the server accepts as authenticated. The potential scope of these requests was limited to querying auxiliary information and certain configuration statuses. Under no circumstances could they generate unauthorised payments via Bizum Pay, nor could they carry out illegitimate activations of the app (which always require access to the customer’s banking channels, thereby protecting them from this type of potential vulnerability). Furthermore, requests are always limited to a set number of attempts and are closely monitored to prevent potential mass queries.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.205 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Unauthenticated exploitation requires the plugin's "Allow posting without logging in" (post_logged_out) option to be enabled; on default installs the vulnerability is exploitable by Subscriber-level users and above.

Improper link resolution in image metadata tarball unpacking in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, and 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with a restricted client certificate to write arbitrary host files as root and execute code on the host via a crafted rootfs symlink in an image metadata tarball.

Exposure of sensitive information in token operation events in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user restricted to a project to gain full server access and cancel pending token operations via capturing certificate or cluster join token secrets broadcast to default project event listeners.

Exposure of sensitive information and missing requestor validation in instance, volume, and snapshot migration operations in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project event or operation read access to read migrating configuration and filesystem data and disrupt the migration via capturing per-connection websocket secrets from operation metadata and racing the migration's data channels.

Configuration injection in virtual machine disk device handling in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with VM creation permissions in a restricted project to bypass low-level VM restrictions and control the root QEMU process via quotes and line breaks in a disk device's guest path.

Exposure of sensitive information in live and stateful migration operations in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project event or operation read access to read a migrating instance's checkpointed runtime state and disrupt the migration via capturing the state connection secret from operation events or queries.

Improper output encoding in Prometheus metrics exposition in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a user controlling a virtual machine to forge host metric labels and break metrics scraping via unescaped guest-controlled filesystem mountpoints and network interface names.

Improper certificate validation in websocket connections in Canonical pylxd before 2.4.3 allows a network attacker to read command stdin and spoof command output via impersonating a remote LXD endpoint.

C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. A crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability within the application. Incorrect authorization in affected versions of network-manager in Ubuntu allows a local attacker with code execution as the whoopsie user to invoke root-restricted D-Bus methods via an Ubuntu-specific D-Bus policy, disrupting network connectivity or altering network configuration.

The Advanced Custom Fields: Font Awesome Field plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'acf[field_klzacffa_iconcls] (profile.php) / acf.profile_icon_class (REST)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping.
